name: NCSA Mosaic graphical web browser
description: A distributed graphical Web browser for networked information, later known for displaying images alongside text.

date.basis: Date or approximate interval stated by the source for this event.

events.statement: NCSA announced X Mosaic 0.5 and made source and binaries available by FTP for several Unix workstation platforms.
events.scope: X Mosaic 0.5 alpha/beta; separate later features are not inferred.

contributions.resource: Announced the 0.5 release and described distribution.

evidence.supports: The preserved mailing-list message identifies Andreessen.
Andreessen’s original announcement describes the release and FTP access.

events.caveats: The January 1993 alpha/beta announcement lists binaries for particular Unix workstation systems; network access and compatible hardware were required. Availability does not establish total user cost or license rights.

date.label: by December 1993
date.basis: NCSA retrospective reports the rate by December, not the precise interval counted.

events.statement: NCSA retrospectively reported more than 5,000 browser downloads per month by December 1993.
events.caveats: Downloads are not distinct users; the retrospective does not specify versions or counting method.

evidence.supports: NCSA reports more than 5,000 downloads per month by December 1993.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated event established in the cited sources for this scoped record; it does not assert global priority.

places.note: NCSA at the University of Illinois.

measures.subject: Mosaic browser downloads by December 1993
measures.conditions: NCSA retrospective; not a count of unique users or particular version.

evidence.supports: Reports more than 5,000 monthly downloads by December 1993.

links.statement: Mosaic was a Web browser for accessing the World Wide Web information system.
links.scope: Web access function, not a claim about every other network feature.

evidence.supports: The release announces a World Wide Web browser.

caveats: Browsers preceded Mosaic. NCSA associates Mosaic generally with inline images, but the 0.5 announcement does not establish the first version with that feature.

research.note: Source-backed initial research; independent review is pending. Independent reader checked Andreessen’s release message and NCSA’s reported monthly-download rate, which is not an individual-user count. Independent reader checked the original X Mosaic announcement and NCSA download retrospective; downloads do not count unique users and the release message does not establish unrestricted licensing.
